version.changelog:
- Expanded skill to support any website or blog, not just filomail.com.
- Generalized references to file paths and directories to be user-configurable (e.g., product context, brand guidelines, internal links map, content plan).
- Clarified instructions for pre-flight and research phases to remove brand-specific requirements.
- No changes to workflow, process, or QA guardrails.

llm.summary: This SEO writing skill is mostly coherent, but it asks agents to run with full execution privileges and bypass normal approval gates for a blog-writing workflow.

dimensions.detail: Shell execution, external URL fetching, third-party source-quality checks, and an external QA runner are plausible for SEO QA, but requiring full exec for the whole writing subagent is not proportionate or narrowly scoped.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The inspected package contains only artifact/SKILL.md and no bundled executable scripts, dependencies, install hooks, or hidden payload files.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill mandates spawning a subagent with security: "full", says approval gates block later phases, and instructs the agent not to ask before running QA, which is broader authority than the workflow clearly requires.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill creates persistent article drafts, research briefs, partial outputs, and QA reports in project directories, which is expected for content production but should be user-visible and path-scoped; no system-level persistence was found.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose, SEO blog writing with research, link verification, and QA, matches most requested actions such as reading project context, writing drafts, checking links, and running a QA script.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing. The workflow is useful for SEO content production, but only run it in a constrained workspace, confirm which files it may read and write, and do not grant full execution privileges unless you trust the referenced QA scripts and the network requests they make.
llm.findings:
[T05] unexpected: Accepted as a material Review concern: artifact lines 16-29 explicitly require full exec permissions and security: "full" to avoid approval gates, despite the workflow needing only scoped link checks and a QA script.
[SQP-1] expected: Downgraded: the broad "any blog article" trigger is overinclusive, but it is consistent with a general blog-writing skill and does not by itself create high-impact security risk.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Accepted for the full-exec subagent requirement because the artifact directly requires unrestricted execution for routine blog QA and link verification.
[SQP-2] expected: Partially accepted but not decisive: incremental draft and recovery writes are normal for article production, though users should know target paths before the skill writes or overwrites content.
[E1] expected: Partially accepted: external link checks and source-quality lookups are purpose-aligned for SEO, but the skill does not clearly gate or scope outbound requests to avoid leaking sensitive drafts, internal URLs, or browsing intent.
[SQP-3] expected: Downgraded: the Chinese title-year section is a readability/localization issue, not evidence of malicious or high-impact behavior.
